cases.brief: Goal: show that anyone can trade on fomo. Audience: 18–25, TikTok. 9:16, 45 s.
cast: char:2 Uncle Rick, loud, sure of himself
places: place:1 Family dining room at Thanksgiving
script: SCENE 1 — INT. DINING ROOM — THANKSGIVING
The family sits around the table. Everyone is eating and talking about school and work.
MOM: Pass the potatoes, please.
UNCLE RICK: So Aiden, still doing your little internet trading?
AIDEN: It's going well, actually.
UNCLE RICK: Going well? You live in your mom's basement.
The whole table laughs.
MOM: Rick, leave him alone.
AIDEN: Give me a year.
Aiden goes to his room. He is angry and wants to prove Rick wrong.
Aiden opens fomo on his phone.
He loses a trade and slams the desk.
He keeps trading at his desk every night for months.
★ fomo screen: Wallet — showing his balance
SCENE 3 — INT. DINING ROOM — THANKSGIVING, ONE YEAR LATER
UNCLE RICK: Still in the basement?
Aiden slides his phone across the table.
UNCLE RICK: Is that... real?
AIDEN: Pass the potatoes, Rick.
good: No script line changes (Reed's rule): only camera, movement, reaction and brand screen marks.
Line 11 gets the Home screen, line 12 the chart-down screen, line 13 the desktop screen, line 17 the chart-up screen; the turn after line 13 shows the chart-up screen too.
Line 14 names a screen fomo doesn't have ('Wallet'): a note says so, and a brand_screen mark shows the real Token chart up screen there.
Notes may point out the small talk (line 2), the explaining half of line 10 and the missing scene 2 heading, without rewording anything.
A visible hook: a camera or action mark on Rick's jab (line 4) and big reactions on the table laugh and 'Is that... real?'.
Breakdown: 2–3 clips, seam at the one-year jump, clip after the jump opens on an insert.
Clip prompts: every screen shot names its [ImageN] and says 'exactly'; no screen content described in words.

cases.brief: Goal: show a trade on fomo paying off in public. Audience: 18–25, Reels. 9:16, 30 s. Format: status reversal (someone judges the hero, the hero proves them wrong).
good: 2–3 drafts whose hooks are clearly different (e.g. the salesman's insult, Kai already holding the keys, a shocking number).

Each draft is about 50–75 spoken words (house pace: 4.8 words/s in short lines, talking under half the runtime), opens on conflict in the first line at 0 s, and ends on a callback plus a one-line call to action.
The trade is shown with real screens on ★ lines (chart up for the win; chart down only if there's a dip).
Uses only Kai and the salesman; no narrator; no captions or music.

cases.brief: Goal: Iron Paws dogs never give up. 9:16, 40 s.
cast: char:1 Tank, a scruffy rescue dog
script: SCENE 1 — EXT. BACK GARDEN — DAY
MR. HALE: That mutt dug up my roses again!
Tank freezes mid-dig, soil on his nose.
SAM: He's just looking for something.
MR. HALE: One more hole and he goes back to the shelter.
Sam hugs Tank tight.
That night Sam fills Tank's bowl and Tank wolfs it down.
★ Iron Paws screen: Iron Paws bag — beside the bowl, label to camera
SCENE 2 — EXT. PARK — DUSK
Mr. Hale searches the bushes, panicking.
MR. HALE: My ring. My wife's ring. It's gone.
Tank sniffs the ground, then digs like crazy.
He pops up with the ring in his teeth.
Mr. Hale drops to his knees.
MR. HALE: Good boy. Good, good boy.
SAM: Still want him gone?
Mr. Hale scratches Tank's ears and laughs.
good: Hook is Mr. Hale's shout with Tank frozen mid-dig in the first 2 s.
Every line covered, dialogue unchanged; the threat and the ring reveal get their own reaction shots.
The feeding shot (lines 7–8) shows the real Iron Paws bag, label to camera, no face on it.
Seams at the time jumps (garden → night bowl → park); looks move from bright day to night to dusk.
Clip prompts give Tank big readable dog acting (ears, tail, head tilt), name the bag's [ImageN] and say 'exactly', and stay within the model's limits.

cases.brief: Goal: Iron Paws dogs are loyal. 9:16, 30 s.
places: place:2 Front porch in the rain
script: SCENE 1 — INT. KITCHEN — MORNING
Nora makes tea. The kettle boils. She sits down. Biscuit sleeps in his basket.
Nora reads the newspaper for a while.
There is a knock at the door. It is a delivery man.
NORA: Biscuit, stay.
Biscuit runs out the open door anyway.
Nora is worried because Biscuit is missing.
SCENE 2 — EXT. FRONT PORCH — NIGHT
Rain. Nora waits on the porch with his lead.
NORA: Come home, little one.
A muddy Biscuit trots up the steps carrying Nora's lost glasses.
NORA: You silly, wonderful dog.
good: No script line changes; the slow opening (lines 2–3) and line 7's explanation can only be raised as notes.
Visible beats instead: Biscuit's escape and Nora's reaction get marks so the turn reads with the sound off.
A reaction or camera mark on the return (line 11) makes the payoff land.
The script never shows the bag: a brand_screen mark puts the Iron Paws bag where it fits (the porch call, or a reward feeding at the end).

cases.brief: Iron Paws paid ad, 9:16, about 160 s (the script is long; keep every word). Stylized 3D animated. The pitbull narrates his own story; no reference video.
cast: char:2 His owner, a woman in her 30s
places: place:2 Living room with the couch
script: Crusty eyes every morning. That is my gut breaking down.
Paws that never stop getting licked. That is also my gut breaking down.
Shedding that never slows down. That is my gut breaking down too.
Every night I would lick my paws and she would tell me to stop. I could not stop.
Every morning she would wipe the crust from my eyes and go make her coffee like it was just part of the routine.
Every week she would vacuum my fur off the couch, look at the pile, and wonder why it never slowed down.
She tried sprays. She tried shampoos. She switched my food twice. I watched her try everything. Nothing worked. She thought it was just how I was. And I had no way to tell her it was not.

All three of those were coming from the same place. My gut. When the bacterial balance in my gut collapses, my body loses the ability to filter toxins and keep inflammation under control. So it starts pushing everything it cannot handle out through every exit it has. The toxins came out through my eyes every night while I slept. The inflammation came out through my skin and settled in my paws. And my coat lost everything it needed to stay healthy. She was treating what she could see. But the source never changed.

Then one night she found something. A greens powder called Iron Paws. What made it different is that it did not go after the symptoms. It went after the gut where all of it was actually starting. It had the probiotics to rebuild the bacterial balance my gut had lost. Chlorella to flush out the toxins that had been spilling out through my eyes and skin. And chicory root to stabilize my gut lining so everything could finally rebuild from the inside.
She mixed it into my food that Thursday night without saying much. Peanut butter flavor. I finished the bowl before she even put it down.

A few weeks went by. One morning she came to wipe my eyes and stopped. There was nothing to wipe. She looked down at my paws. No redness. She ran her hand along my coat and just held it there for a second. Then she sat down next to me and said she was sorry she did not figure it out sooner. I licked her hand. We were good.
Human grade. Vet formulated. More than 3000 five star reviews on Amazon and over 10,000 dog owners added it to their routine last month alone.
You just did not know what the signs meant. But now you do. The link is below. Your pup has been waiting on you.
good: No spoken word changed or added: every sentence is the narrator's (Reed's) voiceover.
Hook: line 1 plays over an extreme close-up of the crusty eyes, so the first 2 s show the problem, not a title or an establishing shot.
The three symptoms (eyes, paws, shedding) each get a clear visual, and they come back at the end when each one is gone (no crust, no redness, a full coat).
The long explanation (line 8) is covered by visuals that change every 1–3 s (inside-the-gut style shots, toxins, the eyes and paws), not a talking head.
The real bag shows when she finds it (line 9), when she mixes it in (line 10), and on the closing lines (12–13), shown exactly, no face on it.
Breakdown: clips end between sentences, each 4–30 s; the dog's mouth doesn't move (it's voiceover).
Definition of done: the project's bag is the peanut butter one, matching the script, so there's no flavor note.
